solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Barb piercing fish soon causing bad suffering

parts.note: a barb or sting, as in a pointed remark
early = soon, before the expected time

explanation.surface: An angler describes a nasty accident: a hook through a fish that soon leaves someone in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barb' looks like a fishing hook to go with the fish, but here it is a cutting remark, a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costing dearly causes serious loss or pain to the one who pays.

clue.text: Sounding harsh about policeman I'm surprised turned back on good judgment

explanation.surface: A startled speaker turns their back on good sense when a policeman appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nous' is everyday British slang for practical good sense. 'On' simply means 'placed next to' in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacophonous describes a harsh, discordant sound.

clue.text: Move beam, changing article for ironwork, primarily

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of 'ironwork'

parts.note: a shaft of light is a beam

indicators.note: marks what the article is exchanged for

parts.note: first letter of ironwork, put in where A was

explanation.surface: An instruction on a building site: move the beam and swap one fitting for some ironwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The builder's picture makes 'beam' a girder, but it is a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shift a thing is to change its position.

clue.text: Unproblematic having no kids

definitions.meaning: issue is the legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A remark that life without children is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' in the sense of children is the old legal term, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of 'issue', problems and offspring, can be absent.

clue.text: Cups turned up in hostel bogs

indicators.note: in a down clue, read the letters from bottom to top
the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of 'hostel' into 'bogs'; read them upward

explanation.surface: Someone finds drinking cups in the toilets of a hostel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bogs' is British slang for toilets, which makes the surface nicely grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Goblets are drinking cups, usually stemmed.

clue.text: Potty revolutionary cycling for some time

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so the letters rotate and the last comes back to the front

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A mad rebel takes up cycling for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as crazy but is the noun: a po is a chamber pot, the British nursery word.
explanation.definitionFit: An era or long stretch of history, which 'some time' loosely covers.

clue.text: Sailor bitten by insect is slowing

explanation.surface: A seaman stung by an insect finds himself slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect has to be a specific kind, the red ant, to split round TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant substance slows a process, such as a fire.

clue.text: Desire bread from abroad

definitions.meaning: bread is slang for money, so a foreign currency: Japan's

explanation.surface: A craving for foreign bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so foreign bread is a foreign currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a craving, and the currency of Japan.

clue.text: Each maid peeled fruit

indicators.note: each word loses its outside letters, like skin from fruit

parts.note: EACH without its first and last letters
MAID without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Each maid peels fruit in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeled' sits naturally with fruit but works on both preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Acai is the berry of a South American palm.

clue.text: Source of virus overlooked in otherwise unobtrusive section of code

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A programmer's warning: the virus was missed, hidden in an innocent-looking piece of code.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface is seamless; 'section of code' is the plain definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A subroutine is a self-contained section of a program.

clue.text: Rush imbibing the French wine

parts.note: a spate is a rush or flood

explanation.surface: Someone hastily gulps down the French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb for hurried drinking, but it is the noun spate.
explanation.definitionFit: Spätlese is a German late-harvest wine.

clue.text: Listen briefly, political party is short of funds

indicators.note: HARK is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A plea for attention: a political party has run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish party, a regular in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British phrase for someone struggling for cash.

clue.text: Damage one covered in plastered neutral colour

indicators.note: drunk, so NEUTRAL is jumbled

explanation.surface: Harm done when someone is splattered with plaster in a beige shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests plasterwork to match 'neutral colour', but it means drunk. The definition is the last word; 'neutral' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a deep blue pigment, first ground from lapis lazuli brought from 'beyond the sea'.

clue.text: Crowded company moved to let one go

parts.note: moved emotionally, impressed; without I it is MPRESSED

explanation.surface: A packed firm is persuaded to lay off a staff member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' reads as relocated, but it means touched emotionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Compressed things are squeezed together, crowded.

clue.text: Each year small group nakedly abuse nationalist

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
to give stick is to criticise; stripped to TIC

explanation.surface: An annual gathering of a few people who strip off and hurl abuse at a nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' in the sense of abuse or harsh criticism is British idiom ('take a lot of stick').
explanation.definitionFit: Here nationalist is the adjective: devoted to one's country.

clue.text: Not scared to go round city

indicators.note: the letters turn about into a new order

explanation.surface: A brave traveller willing to tour a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster is a town, now a city, in South Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this South Yorkshire town was granted city status in 2022.

clue.text: Popular type not completely creative

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A description of a sociable sort who is only half artistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the two words, POPUL|AR TY|PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily creative.

clue.text: Cry over piquant wraps

indicators.note: to wrap something is to enclose it, so the word for piquant closes round the letter for over

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over spicy wraps at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraps' looks like food to go with piquant, but it is the container verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an owl's call or a burst of laughter, both kinds of cry.

clue.text: Dreadful thing stopping witness attending since

explanation.surface: Something awful prevented a witness from coming to court.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides as the last word, a humble conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Seeing that' and 'since' both mean 'because'.

clue.text: One charming rogue in Crete

indicators.note: something gone rogue has broken from its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charming rogue on holiday in Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One charming rogue' reads as a unit, but 'rogue' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticer charms or lures others.

clue.text: Perceives sixth sense that is singular

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's sixth sense is unique.
explanation.walkthrough: Every piece is a standard abbreviation strung in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, perceive.

clue.text: Stop exhausted outside shelter to rest

indicators.note: the emptied word sits on the outside, its two letters flanking the shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A worn-out walker halts beside a shelter to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop exhausted' reads as someone too tired to go on, but 'exhausted' empties the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sleep is the fullest kind of rest.

clue.text: Transport returned in the westbound lane of airway

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters read in reverse
the reversed transport is placed inside 'the'
in an across clue, going west is right to left

explanation.surface: A car is seen driving the wrong way on a westbound lane.
explanation.walkthrough: The motoring surface hides a medical definition at the end: 'of airway' needs an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracheal means relating to the trachea, the windpipe or airway.

clue.text: Treasure group of nomads picked up

indicators.note: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: a horde is a nomadic tribe or throng

explanation.surface: A band of wanderers comes across a treasure trove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' pretends the nomads collected the treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, treasure can mean a stockpile of valuables, which is exactly this.

clue.text: Do exploit male recruits regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: An order to take advantage of the men being enlisted from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb, but it is the noun, a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Do' is informal shorthand for hairdo; this layered style was popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Blunder is end for white bishop

indicators.note: only the last letter of 'white' is used

parts.note: Rt Rev, Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A chess comment: losing the white bishop is a mistake that ends the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is false: the bishop is a churchman, RR being the Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to make a mistake.

clue.text: Keen to help five dons

explanation.surface: Five university lecturers are eager to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like Oxbridge teachers, but it is the verb, puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean eager and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Bird to shake crest on overturned snare

parts.note: the crest of a hill is a ridge

explanation.surface: A bird ruffles its crest over an upturned trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The crest reads as feathers, but it is the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock partridge is a game bird of southern Europe.
